title: Walkthru-Indices
description: A suite of four global planetary indices — terrain (elevation, slope, aspect, TRI, TPI), building density and volume, SSP2 population projections (2025–2100), and near-real-time weather forecasts — aggregated onto a common H3 hexagonal grid at multiple resolutions. All indices are derived from GEDTM-30m, Global Building Atlas, WorldPop SSP, and NOAA AI-NWP source data and stored as Apache Parquet partitioned by H3 resolution. Every index shares a single h3_index key, enabling cross-dataset spatial joins in a single SQL query.

## README.md
# walkthru-earth / indices

Open planetary indices that turn raw scientific data into a single, H3-hexagonal grid anyone can query with one SQL statement. Every index shares the same cell ID (`h3_index`), so joining terrain + buildings + population + weather is a one-line `JOIN ON h3_index`.

**Why?** Cities shape how people feel — but the data to prove it is scattered across dozens of agencies, formats, and projections. We unify it into one queryable, open layer so researchers, planners, and communities can finally see the full picture. Read more: [walkthru.earth/hormones-cities](https://walkthru.earth/hormones-cities)

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Raw["Raw sources"]
        DEM_RAW["GEDTM-30m\n(30 m GeoTIFF)"]
        GBA_RAW["Global Building Atlas\n(2.75 B polygons)"]
        WP_RAW["WorldPop SSP\n(1 km rasters)"]
        NOAA_RAW["NOAA AI-NWP\n(0.25° NetCDF)"]
    end

    subgraph H3["H3 conversion"]
        direction TB
        DT["dem-terrain\nelev · slope · aspect · TRI · TPI"]
        BI["walkthru-building-index\ndensity · height · volume"]
        PI["walkthru-pop-index\n2025 → 2100 projections"]
        WI["walkthru-weather-index\ntemp · wind · precip · pressure"]
    end

    DEM_RAW --> DT
    GBA_RAW --> BI
    WP_RAW --> PI
    NOAA_RAW --> WI
    DT -. topo corrections .-> WI

    subgraph S3["s3://…/walkthru-earth/"]
        T[dem-terrain/v2/h3/]
        B[indices/building/v2/h3/]
        P[indices/population/v2/]
        W[indices/weather/]
    end

    DT --> T
    BI --> B
    PI --> P
    WI --> W

    T -. JOIN h3_index .-> Q((Query))
    B -. JOIN .-> Q
    P -. JOIN .-> Q
    W -. JOIN .-> Q
```

## Indices

| Index | What | H3 Res | Update | Size |
|-------|------|--------|--------|------|
| **[dem-terrain](https://source.coop/walkthru-earth/dem-terrain)** | Elevation, slope, aspect, TRI, TPI from GEDTM-30m | 1–10 | One-time | ~287 GB, 10.5 B cells |
| **[walkthru-building-index](https://source.coop/walkthru-earth/indices)** | Density, height, footprint, volume from 2.75 B buildings | 3–8 | One-time | ~2.6 GB, 53 M cells |
| **[walkthru-pop-index](https://source.coop/walkthru-earth/indices)** | SSP2 projections 2025–2100 (16 timesteps) from WorldPop | 1–8 | One-time | ~4.5 GB, 44 M cells |
| **[walkthru-weather-index](https://source.coop/walkthru-earth/indices)** | Temperature, wind, precip, pressure + topo corrections | 0–5 | Every 12 h | ~3.6 GB / forecast |

All datasets: [Apache Parquet](https://parquet.apache.org/), ZSTD compression, sorted by `h3_index`.
- **v2 (recommended):** `h3_index` is BIGINT (int64) — no `geometry`, `lat`, `lon`, or `area_km2` columns (all derivable from the H3 index via DuckDB's h3 extension). Sorted by int64 for better compression and fast range-based spatial queries.
- **v1 (legacy):** `h3_index` is VARCHAR (hex string) with native Parquet 2.11+ GEOMETRY and `lat`/`lon`/`area_km2` columns.

## Quick start

```sql
-- DuckDB: join buildings + population in one query (v2 — BIGINT h3_index, no geometry)
INSTALL httpfs;  LOAD httpfs;
INSTALL h3 FROM community; LOAD h3;
SET s3_region = 'us-west-2';

SELECT b.h3_index,
       h3_h3_to_string(b.h3_index) AS h3_hex,          -- hex string for deck.gl
       h3_cell_to_lat(b.h3_index)  AS lat,              -- derive lat on the fly
       h3_cell_to_lng(b.h3_index)  AS lon,              -- derive lon on the fly
       b.building_count, b.building_density,
       p.pop_2025, p.pop_2050,
       (b.building_count::FLOAT / NULLIF(p.pop_2025, 0))::DECIMAL(6,3) AS bldg_per_person
FROM read_parquet('s3://us-west-2.opendata.source.coop/walkthru-earth/indices/building/v2/h3/h3_res=5/data.parquet') b
JOIN read_parquet('s3://us-west-2.opendata.source.coop/walkthru-earth/indices/population/v2/scenario=SSP2/h3_res=5/data.parquet') p
  ON b.h3_index = p.h3_index                            -- BIGINT join — fast
WHERE p.pop_2025 > 10000
ORDER BY bldg_per_person DESC
LIMIT 10;
```

## S3 layout

```
s3://us-west-2.opendata.source.coop/walkthru-earth/
├── dem-terrain/
│   ├── v1/h3/h3_res={1-10}/data.parquet          ← legacy (VARCHAR h3, has geometry/lat/lon)
│   └── v2/h3/h3_res={1-10}/data.parquet          ← recommended (BIGINT h3, lean schema)
└── indices/
    ├── building/
    │   ├── v1/h3/h3_res={3-8}/data.parquet        ← legacy
    │   ├── v2/h3/h3_res={3-8}/data.parquet        ← recommended
    │   └── globalbuildingatlas/zoomlevel={2-14}/data*.parquet
    ├── population/
    │   ├── v1/scenario=SSP2/h3_res={1-8}/data.parquet  ← legacy
    │   └── v2/scenario=SSP2/h3_res={1-8}/data.parquet  ← recommended
    └── weather/
        └── model=GraphCast_GFS/date=YYYY-MM-DD/hour={0,12}/h3_res={0-5}/data.parquet
```
